dataset: Jigsaw Toxic Comment Held-Out Test Set

disparities.statistical_gap_verdict: Statistically significant performance disparity observed across comment length cohorts. Short comments exhibit higher FNR due to lexical sparsity, whereas long comments accumulate higher FPR due to polysemous trigger words.

research_questions.q1_performance_difference: Yes. F1-score varies meaningfully across comment lengths, with medium comments achieving the most balanced trade-off.
research_questions.q2_largest_differences: The largest disparity appears in False Negative Rate (FNR) on very short comments and False Positive Rate (FPR) on long comments.
research_questions.q3_sufficient_data: Yes. Each cohort contains over 500 samples with positive cases, yielding non-degenerate 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
research_questions.q4_frequent_errors: Short comments suffer from missed toxic slurs without sufficient context (FN), while long comments trigger false alarms on quoted or discussed offensive terms (FP).
research_questions.q5_limitations: Comment length is an extrinsic linguistic feature rather than a protected demographic attribute; bag-of-words vectorization lacks long-range co-reference resolution.
